$comment: Which samples in samples/workflows/ become recipe pages under docs/recipes/. Run `pnpm --filter @ai-orchestrator/docs gen:recipes` (the docs build runs it). Each entry: sample (file name), slug (page name), title (<= 54 chars; the page title adds ' | L2M'), description (<= 155 chars), tags (lower case; they become the filters on /recipes/), summary (Markdown, a short paragraph on what it does and when to use it), related (glossary slugs, optional), docs (further reading inside the docs, optional).

recipes.title: MCP agent quickstart: an agent with two MCP tools
recipes.description: A ready-to-import L2M workflow: one agent with a chat model and two MCP tools, a clock and a calculator. Runs without API keys on a fresh install.
recipes.summary: The smallest useful agent: a manual trigger starts one Agent Orchestrator node, which answers with the help of two MCP tools from the bundled mock MCP server, `get_current_time` and `calculator`. The chat model is the built-in echo provider, so it runs with no API key. Use it to see the agent loop and its tool calls, then swap the echo provider for a real model and the mock server for your own MCP server.

docs.text: Build your first MCP agent in 5 min

recipes.title: Supervisor and worker agents: a two-worker swarm
recipes.description: A ready-to-import L2M workflow: a Supervisor agent delegates to a researcher and a calculator worker, each with its own model and MCP tools. No API keys.
recipes.summary: A Supervisor node coordinates two worker agents. The researcher has an MCP knowledge-base lookup tool; the computer has a calculator and a clock. The Supervisor sees each worker as one tool and decides which to call for each step. Every agent uses the built-in echo provider and the bundled mock MCP server, so it runs with no API key. Use it as the starting point when one agent's tool list gets too long or its job splits into roles.
